function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference “starter kit” for a **Startup Statistics API** – i.e. a set of REST endpoints that let developers pull structured information about private companies (“startups”) such as founding year, sector, employee count, latest round size & valuation, revenue estimates, product stack, etc. > ⚠️ If you’re looking for *existing* commercial services, see the section at the end of this post where I point out the most popular paid APIs (CrunchBase Pro, PitchBook, CB Insight, AngelList, etc.). > > For those who want to roll their own, the table below gives you everything you’ll need to define, document, test and deploy a simple yet production‑ready service. --- ## 1️⃣ Core Endpoints | Method | Endpoint | Purpose | Sample Response | |--------|----------|---------|----------------| | `GET` | `/api/startups/` | Retrieve all available metadata for a single company. | ```json
{
"id":"123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
"name":"Acme Corp.",
"founded":2018,
"industry":["FinTech","Payments"],
"employees":{"min":10,"max":50},"website":"https://acmecorp.io",
"valuation_usd":250_000_000,
"funding":[{"stage":"Series B","amount_usd":75_000_000,"date":"2023-04-15"}],
"revenue_estimate_usd_per_annum":30_000_000}
``` | | `GET` | `/api/startups` | List startups with optional filters + paging. | ```json
{"page":1,"per_page":20,"total_pages":34,"results":[…]}
``` | | `GET` | `/api/startups/search` | Full‑text search across name, tagline, description, etc. | ```json
{"q":"blockchain","count":42,"items":[ … ]}
``` | | `GET` | `/api/startups//timeline` | Chronological events (founders added, rounds closed, hires). | ```json
[{"event":"Seed Round","value_usd":500_000,"date":"2019-02-01"}, …]
``` | ### Optional Filters (for `/api/startups`) ``` ?country= &city= &state= §or= &min_funding_usd= &max_employees= &page=&per_page= ``` ### Pagination Strategy * Default `per_page`: 25 * Max allowed `per_page`: 100 * Return meta fields (`next`, `prev`, `last`) so clients can navigate easily. --- ## 2️⃣ Authentication & Rate Limiting | Auth Type | How to obtain | Header | Notes | |-----------|---------------|--------|-------| | API Key | Sign‑up → Dashboard → Create key | `Authorization: Bearer ` | One key per developer account; rotate when hitting quota. | | OAuth2 | Standard flow (client_id/client_secret) | `Authorization: Bearer ` | Useful for enterprise customers needing granular scopes. | #### Rate Limits | Plan | Requests/minute | Burst Capacity | |------|-----------------|----------------| | Free | 60 | 120 | | Basic | 300 | 600 | | Premium | Unlimited (soft cap 2000/min) | 4000 | When exceeding the limit, return `429 Too Many Requests` with `Retry-After`. --- ## 3️⃣ Example Code Snippets ### Python (requests) ```python import os, json, requests BASE_URL = "https://demo.startupstats.api.example.org/api" def _get(endpoint, params=None): resp = requests.get( f"{BASE_URL}{endpoint}", headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {os.getenv('STARTUP_API_KEY')}"}, timeout=10, params=params ) resp.raise_for_status() return resp.json() # Get a specific startup company = _get("/startups/123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000") print(company["name"]) # Search hits = _get("/startups/search", {"q": "fintech"}) print(f"Found {len(hits['items'])} fintech firms.") ``` ### Node.js (axios) ```js const axios = require("axios"); async function lookup(id){ const res = await axios.get(`https://demo.startupstats.api.example.org/api/startups/${id}`, { headers:{ Authorization:`Bearer ${process.env.STARTUP_API_KEY}` } }); console.log(res.data.name); } lookup("123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"); ``` ### curl ```bash curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ "https://demo.startupstats.api.example.org/api/startups?sector=healthcare,min_funding_usd=50000" ``` --- ## 4️⃣ Typical Payload Fields | Field | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `id` | UUID | Unique internal ID | | `name` | String | Legal/company name | | `aliases` | Array[String] | Former names, ticker symbols | | `description` | Text | Short blurb | | `founded` | Int | Year founded | | `location` | Object `{ country, city, region }` | | `industries` | Array[String] | Primary sectors | | `team_size` | Object `{ min:int,max:int }` | | `employee_count_at_date(date)` | int | | `funding` | Array[Object] | `{ stage, amount_usd, currency, date, investors[] }` | | `latest_valuation_usd` | Number | | `revenues` | Array[Object] | `{ fiscal_year, amount_usd, currency }` | | `product_stack` | Array[String] | Tech used (AWS, Docker, React…) | | `social_links` | Object `{ twitter,url,linkedin,…}` | | `logo_url` | String | | `status` | Enum `"operational"`|"bankrupt"| ...| Feel free to add/remove fields based on your domain needs. --- ## 5️⃣ Building Your Own Dataset If you decide to create your own database rather than rely on third‑party feeds, here’s a minimal pipeline: | Step | Tool | What You Do | |------|------|--------------| | Scrape | BeautifulSoup / Playwright | Pull press releases, investor pages, CrunchBase public cards | | Parse | spaCy NER | Extract founders’ names, dates, locations | | Validate | DuckDB / PostgreSQL | Store raw HTML + parsed JSON | | Enrich | Alpha Vantage / Google Places | Add financial ratios, office addresses | | Expose | FastAPI / Flask | Wrap DB queries into REST endpoints | | Cache | Redis | Keep hot results under 1 second latency | | Monitor | Prometheus/Grafana | Track uptime, error rates, query times | A typical ingestion job runs nightly, updates new funding announcements, adds newly registered domains, and flags stale records after 90 days without activity. --- ## 6️⃣ Existing Commercial Services | Service | Pricing Tier | Notable Features | Docs Link | |---------|--------------|------------------|------------| | **CrunchBase Pro** | $99/mo | Funding history, ownership trees, advanced filtering | https://data.crunchbase.com/docs | | **PitchBook** | Custom quotes | Valuations, M&A comps, detailed financials | https://pitchbook.com/help | | **CB Insights** | Custom | Market maps, competitive landscape, AI‑driven alerts | https://www.cbinsights.com/support/documentation | | **AngelList API** | Free tier | Job listings, fundraising status | https://angel.co/api | | **OpenCorporates** | Freemium | Corporate registry worldwide | https://opencorporates.com/developers | | **DataFox (now part of Oracle)** | Enterprise | Real‑time corporate intelligence | https://oracle.com/datafox | These platforms usually offer both **REST** and **GraphQL** interfaces, along with bulk CSV downloads for offline analytics. --- ## 7️⃣ Quick Checklist Before Launch 1. **Schema Design** – Decide mandatory vs optional fields; keep versioned URLs (`/v1/...`). 2. **Auth Flow** – Issue short‑lived tokens; support IP whitelisting for high‑volume partners. 3. **Caching Layer** – CDN edge caching for static assets (logos), Redis for dynamic lookups. 4. **Monitoring** – Log each request, track latency buckets, alert on >95th percentile spikes. 5. **Compliance** – GDPR: allow users to delete personal data; CCPA opt‑out mechanisms. 6. **Documentation** – Swagger/OpenAPI spec; auto‑generate Postman collection. Once you’ve got the first two endpoints live, iterate fast—add more metrics (burn rate, runway, churn) once you validate demand. --- Happy coding! 🚀 Let me know if you’d like help wiring up a demo instance, writing unit tests, or integrating with a front‑end framework.
